notas_ingenieria.titulo: Chimney or squirrel? Clearing up a robot's fuzzy memory by comparing images from different angles

A new study shows how artificial intelligence could help narrow that search before production testing begins.

notas_ingenieria.titulo: Electronics-free artificial reflex reproduces knee-jerk and enables bipedal walking
notas_ingenieria.resumen: When a doctor taps just below your kneecap, your lower leg kicks forward automatically. This knee-jerk reflex is one example of the reflexes that play an essential role in human motor control. Now, researchers at Tohoku University have developed a reflex module for musculoskeletal robots that works without electronic sensors or circuits. Using this module, the team reproduced the knee-jerk reflex in a robot and generated bipedal walking.

notas_ingenieria.titulo: Harnessing atomic structure to advance next-generation memory storage
notas_ingenieria.resumen: The growth of artificial intelligence has increased demand for more efficient data storage.
